transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-10-21 14:30 UTC | Duration: 52m | Attendees: Lena (Redwood AE), Marcus (Redwood SE), Priya (CISO, Solaris), Tom (Head of Platform), Maya (Staff SRE)

Summary: Quick security review focused on audit logs and admin activity capture. Customer wants clarity on what events are logged, export options to SIEM, retention, and encryption/KMS controls for logs. Redwood to provide sample export and schedule PoC to validate SIEM ingest.

Topics: audit log schema, admin actions captured, export endpoints, SIEM integration, retention tiers, KMS/HSM encryption, RBAC/SSO audit hooks, compliance evidence (SOC2/ISO).

[00:00] Lena: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'll kick us off. lotus sorry, lena from redwood inference, im the ae on this account. we have marcus from engineering who can dig into log specifics.
[00:25] Priya: great, thanks. quick context — Solaris is consolidating audit streams into Splunk and needs to know exactly what Redwood captures for admin activity and whether there's any PII in logs, retention, and how to export. timeline is Q4 compliance review.
[00:48] Marcus: thanks priya. high level — our audit logs capture admin actions (user invites, role changes, api key creation/revocation), auth events (sso/saml logins, failure reason), model deploys and rollouts, config changes, tenant-level data access requests, and system-level alerts. we also log request metadata like request id, model variant, region and approximate token counts.
[01:20] Tom: do you capture prompt contents or user-generated content in audit logs? that's a big one for us.
[01:33] Marcus: we do not include full prompt texts in admin/audit logs by default. the audit stream includes request ids and pointers (log ids) that can be cross-referenced with telemetry in a permissions-controlled store. customers on dedicated/private can opt-in for verbatim request logging for debugging, but that's disabled by default for hosted.
[02:00] Maya: and retention? we need 365 days for banking audit. can you do that out of the box?
[02:09] Marcus: retention tiers are configurable; hosted defaults to 90 days, we offer 90/365/730 tiers. long-term retention is an add-on; we can also export raw logs to an S3 bucket (or object store) you manage for indefinite retention.
[02:35] Priya: export format — is it CloudTrail style or custom JSON?
[02:42] Marcus: we send newline-delimited JSON with a well-documented schema. it's CloudTrail-ish in fields (timestamp, eventName, principal, sourceIP, requestId) but includes redwood-specific fields like model_version, route, and deployment_scope. we'll share the schema CSV.
[03:05] Priya: encryption at rest and in transit? KMS?
[03:12] Marcus: logs in transit use TLS. at rest we're using AES-256. for hosted customers we manage keys by default; we support customer-managed keys (CMK) via AWS KMS and can integrate with HSM for private deployments. note: we sometimes say KMS/HSN in some docs — that's a transcription typo — it's KMS/HSM.
[03:45] Tom: for SOC2 evidence, do you provide pre-built reports showing admin activity across time ranges?
[03:53] Lena: yes, we have an audit-log dashboard and exportable reports; we can pull slices for auditors. we also provide event-level exports for e-discovery.
[04:12] Priya: how about RBAC changes — do you capture role mapping and policy diffs?
[04:20] Marcus: we log role assignments, policy attach/detach, and admin UI changes. we capture the before/after state for policy diffs in the audit event payload. small caveat: the diff payload is truncated if huge; for full diffs we advise using the export API.
[04:48] Maya: SIEM integration — can you push into Splunk/Datadog/Sumo? or do we need to pull?
[04:57] Marcus: two options — push via HTTP collector (we can post to your endpoint) or you can configure our export to S3 and have your SIEM pull from there. for real-time alerts we support webhook streaming and Kafka topics for dedicated customers.
[05:20] Priya: any PII in IP addresses or user identifiers — are they hashed?
[05:26] Marcus: IPs are logged (sourceIP) for security purposes; we can enable hashing/pseudonymization on request for compliance. user ids are internal identifiers; we can map to customer-controlled IDs in the export.
[05:48] Tom: what's the SLA around log delivery and retention guarantees?
[05:55] Lena: delivery is best-effort for hosted but we have SLA-backed guarantees for Dedicated customers. retention guarantees depend on the plan and add-ons. we'll include the specific contract language in the docs we send.
[06:15] Priya: audit log tamper-proofing — do you support immutability or append-only stores?
[06:22] Marcus: for hosted we maintain write-once logs and internal checksums. for stronger guarantees you can export to your own WORM-enabled S3 bucket or use our dedicated offering where we can configure HSM-backed signing of events.
[06:45] Maya: about admin activity — how granular is console vs API logging? e.g. who clicked approve vs who called via API?
[06:54] Marcus: we log both with different eventName fields — console actions include actor_user_agent and session id; API calls include API key id or OAuth principal. cross-correlation fields let you tie them together.
[07:18] Priya: are there rate limits or costs for continuous exports?
[07:24] Lena: exports can be batched. there are egress charges and export pricing tiers. we'll provide the pricing matrix.
[07:40] Tom: for private deployments, can we restrict encryption to our KMS only?
[07:45] Marcus: yes, private deployments let you manage keys exclusively; hosted supports CMK but Redwood still has admin access for operational tasks unless contractually restricted.
[08:05] Priya: what about SSO audit hooks — can we tie into our IdP to get SAML assertions?
[08:12] Marcus: we log SAML assertion IDs and outcomes. we don't store full assertion XML in logs by default, but can include assertion references for debug if requested under a controlled opt-in.
[08:35] Maya: can we do a short PoC where we ingest a day's worth of logs into Splunk?
[08:40] Lena: yes — we'll share schema and a sample export. Marcus will prepare the sample export and we'll schedule the PoC.
[09:00] Tom: curious — any known gotchas for model-level events, like token counts inflating logs?
[09:07] Marcus: we log approximate token counts; if you enable verbose request logging that can substantially increase volume. we recommend sampling verbose logs or routing them to your object store.
[09:30] Priya: last question — do you log admin impersonation or session hijack attempts?
[09:36] Marcus: we have anomaly detection alerts for suspicious sessions and record session revocations, concurrent login alerts, and failed MFA attempts. those events are part of the audit stream.
[09:58] Lena: ok great — recap next steps: lena to send SOC2/ISO docs, marcus sample export and schema, schedule PoC with maya, provide pricing and contract language for retention and CMK.
[10:15] Priya: perfect, thank you. that answers a lot.

End of transcript.
